kind: primary-statistic registration for an instrument property
subject: the direction of l1_weight -> L0 in the transcoder-adapters family

not_a_hypothesis_test.statement: This is descriptive statistics of an instrument property. It is NOT a research hypothesis test and it does NOT consume any part of the multiple-testing budget.
not_a_hypothesis_test.why: the quantity described is a property of the measuring apparatus, decided before and independently of any accuracy measurement; it enters no estimand and licenses no scientific claim

why_the_layers_are_a_paired_unit.statement: The two checkpoints share an architecture and a layer indexing, so layer l of one corresponds to layer l of the other. The 28 layers are therefore a paired unit.
why_the_layers_are_a_paired_unit.same_principle_as_the_study: this is the same principle the study already applies to items: compare within the pair, then aggregate, rather than aggregating each arm separately and differencing the summaries
why_the_layers_are_a_paired_unit.why_mean_and_median_over_layers_are_wron: both are UNPAIRED summaries. They discard the layer correspondence and are dominated by the order-of-magnitude tail at layers 26 and 27, where layer 27 alone differs by roughly 19 features per token - enough to flip the sign of the unpaired mean by itself.

registered_primary_statistic.statistic: the per-layer paired difference L0_c(l) - L0_primary(l), across l = 0..27
registered_primary_statistic.primary_object_for_reporting: the per-layer L0 curve, both checkpoints on one figure

demoted_to_descriptive.must_be_labelled: dominated by the layer 26 and 27 tail

measured_result.median_paired_ratio_supports: prose, since the ratio is below 1

the_two_registered_tests_disagree.finding: The sign test reaches p = 0.0125 and supports the prose direction. The Wilcoxon signed-rank does NOT reach significance at alpha = 0.05, returning p = 0.127. Both were registered, so both are reported; reporting only the significant one would be selective reporting.
the_two_registered_tests_disagree.why_they_disagree: The sign test counts direction only and is magnitude-free. Wilcoxon weights each layer by the rank of its absolute difference, so it is magnitude-sensitive. Layers 26 and 27 differ enormously in the TABLE direction - layer 27 alone by about 19 features per token - so those two layers receive the top ranks and pull the signed-rank statistic back toward the null.
the_two_registered_tests_disagree.consequence_for_the_conclusion: The Wilcoxon remains partially vulnerable to exactly the tail that motivated this registration, whereas the sign test does not. That is a reason to prefer the sign test HERE, but it is a reason stated before the conclusion is drawn rather than after, and it does not make the Wilcoxon result disappear.
the_two_registered_tests_disagree.honest_strength_of_evidence: The direction claim rests on the sign test and on the median paired ratio of 0.6685, which agree. It is NOT corroborated by the magnitude-weighted test. The evidence for the direction is therefore real but not overwhelming, and the conclusion is registered at that strength and no higher.

registered_conclusion.conclusion: The README prose is right and the README table is wrong: higher l1_weight produces LOWER L0, meaning a sparser adapter.
registered_conclusion.prose_direction_is_also_the_physically_c: a larger L1 penalty should sparsify, which is what the prose says and the table denies
registered_conclusion.the_readme_table_may_no_longer_be_used: OD-005 forbids using the table's nominal values in place of measurement when selecting the sensitivity arm

claim_ceiling: This describes the behaviour of an instrument on a data slice. It is not evidence about J-space, about distillation, or about reasoning, and it is not a scientific result.
